subject: Urgent: RoadRunner production latency & errors after model upgrade
messages:
From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@roadrunnerlogistics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@roadrunnerlogistics.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p95 spike and errors after 'v2.1-q4' rollout — urgent

Jordan —

We just observed a pretty severe regression in production right after you pushed the v2.1 / q4 quant profile yesterday night. Key symptoms: p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~950ms, error rate rose from ~0.8% to ~5.2%, and sustained throughput per replica dropped ~30%. The failure manifests as 500s and timeouts for longer prompts (>512 tokens) and garbled responses in a small sample.

This is affecting our routing and customer SLAs — we've already rerouted a small percentage of traffic but our dashboards are still showing elevated error counts. Can you please:
- Confirm whether v2.1-q4 was rolled to our production pool last night
- Provide immediate mitigation or rollback plan (we need something within the next 6 hours)
- Point us to a contact for exec escalation — our CTO is asking for an update.

I've attached a short perf-sample and logs (perf-sample-20260811.json, perf-log-20260810.tar.gz).

Thanks,
Ethan
Platform & Data Lead
RoadRunner Logistics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@roadrunnerlogistics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike and errors after 'v2.1-q4' rollout — urgent

Thanks Jordan, Ethan — initial findings below from a quick triage. I'm dropping the short technical summary and next-action steps.

Symptom summary (observed in your perf-sample and our cluster metrics):
- Latency: p95 ~950ms on sequences >512; p50/p90 less impacted
- Errors: 500s tied to OOM & kernel fallback exceptions in a subset of replicas
- Throughput: per-replica tokens/sec down ~25-35% after q4 activation

Preliminary root cause hypothesis:
- The q4 quant profile introduced a fused attention kernel that is faster in short-sequence benchmarks but triggers a different memory layout for KV caches on sequences with many past tokens. For RoadRunner's workload (many long-history prompts + caching), we've hit a path where the runtime starts spilling KV segments to host memory and falling back to slower kernels. That causes sudden latency spikes and intermittent errors when memory thresholds are crossed.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (ordered by invasiveness):
1) Roll your pool back to the last-known-good model/variant (v2.0 / q3) — fastest and most predictable.
2) Disable q4 on your pool and force the runtime to use the non-fused kernels (config toggle) — near-immediate (minutes) but slightly higher steady-state token-cost.
3) Apply an adaptive prefix-pruning knob in routing to reduce average sequence length as a temporary throttle (mitigates p95 but changes outputs).
4) Scale burst capacity (add replicas) — buys time but not a fix.

I've attached a short mitigation-playbook.md with the exact CLI and API commands to execute 1) and 2). If you want us to do the rollback, we can schedule a zero-downtime pin-and-rollback; estimate 45–90 minutes to fully revert and validate across your pool.

Root cause action items (follow-up):
- We'll capture a repro trace and file an infra bug to fix the fused kernel path to avoid the KV spill condition.
- We'll add a regression test to the rollout pipeline for long-sequence workloads.

Ethan — tell me which immediate mitigation you'd prefer (1 or 2) and we'll execute.

Marissa Cole
Senior SW Eng, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation-playbook.md

--

Subject: Exec update / rollback in progress — RoadRunner

Team — quick update for the record and execs.

What happened: v2.1 with q4 quant profile was staged to RoadRunner's pool at 02:00 UTC and caused a kernel/runtime path that increases KV-memory spill for long prompts. That produced p95 latency spikes and intermittent 500s.

What we're doing now:
- Executing pinned rollback to v2.0 across all RoadRunner production replicas (Marissa is leading) — estimated complete by 16:15 PDT (rolling validation ongoing)
- Disabling q4 auto-rollouts to any RoadRunner pools until we complete the postmortem
- Rishi to open an SLA credit request intake with sales ops and provide a single point of contact for Ethan's execs

Next steps (post-rollback):
- 72-hour hotfix window to produce a regression patch and a reproducible test; target: root-cause PR within 48 hours, fix in canary within 72 hours.
- Postmortem distributed to RoadRunner and internal execs within 5 business days.

I'll coordinate the exec contact: cc'ing Rishi to take the lead on credits and exec comms. Ethan/Asha — I will update you as soon as rollback validation is green.

Jordan Blake
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
